title: Classic Béchamel White Sauce
summary: A pale butter and flour roux slowly loosened with whole milk and simmered until velvety, seasoned with white pepper and nutmeg.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Make a pale roux
steps.text: Melt the butter in the saucepan over medium-low heat, keeping it from colouring. Whisk in the flour and cook for 1-2 min, stirring, until it smells toasty rather than raw.

steps.title: Add the milk gradually
steps.text: Pour in a little milk and whisk until smooth before adding more. The paste will clump at first, then relax into a thin sauce once all the milk is in.

steps.title: Simmer to thicken
steps.text: Bring the sauce to a gentle bubble, whisking and reaching into the edges of the pan, and cook for 5-8 min until it coats the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Season
steps.text: Take the pan off the heat and add the salt, white pepper and a grating of nutmeg.

steps.title: Use
steps.text: Use it straight away in lasagne, gratins or croque monsieur, or serve it in a warm jug.

tips: Warm the milk first if you like; it blends in a little faster.
If lumps appear, whisk hard off the heat or blitz briefly with a stick blender.
For a thicker sauce for binding or soufflés, use 40 g each of butter and flour.
White pepper keeps the sauce spotless, but black pepper is fine.
storage: Press baking paper onto the surface to stop a skin forming, cool, then refrigerate for up to 3 days. Reheat gently, whisking in a splash of milk. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
